intro: Sentence-final じゃないか (polite じゃないですか, formal ではないか, casual じゃない and じゃん) is not a negative. It holds a fact up as obvious and asks the listener to see it: "isn't it!", "you know ...", "look, it's ...!". Depending on context it expresses surprise, a reminder, a reproach, or, after a volitional verb, a rousing "let's".

skills.rule: Put じゃないか after a plain form (a noun without だ) to present a fact as obvious: surprise ("why, it's X!"), a reminder ("you know X") or a reproach ("I told you, didn't I!").
skills.explain:
Despite its shape, this じゃない negates nothing. なんだ、田中さんじゃないか means "Oh, it's Tanaka!" and 言ったじゃない means "I told you, didn't I!". Said with a falling tone, it asserts: surprise at a discovery (おいしいじゃないか, hey, this is good), reproach (遅いじゃないか, you're late!), a reminder of something the listener knows (駅前に本屋があるじゃないですか), and, after a volitional verb, a call to action (やろうじゃないか, let's do it!).

It attaches to the plain form with no だ: 学生じゃないか, 静かじゃないか, 高いじゃないか, 来たじゃないか. After verbs and い-adjectives a real negative changes the word (高くない, 来なかった), so おいしいじゃない can only be the particle. After nouns and な-adjectives the shapes match (静かじゃない: "it's not quiet" or "why, it's quiet!"); context and the falling, emphatic tone decide.

Register: じゃん is casual and very common; じゃないですか is polite but, overused for your own opinions, sounds pushy; ではないか belongs to speeches and writing.
patterns: [plain form, no だ] じゃないか / じゃない

examples.jp: なんだ、田中[たなか]さん{じゃないか}。
このラーメン、おいしい{じゃないか}。
だから、言[い]った{じゃない}。
その服[ふく]、いい{じゃん}。
駅[えき]の前[まえ]に本屋[ほんや]がある{じゃないですか}。
examples.en: You know the bookshop in front of the station?

examples.jp: みんなで最後[さいご]までやろう{じゃないか}。
examples.en: Let's all see this through to the end!

contrast.note: だろう is a guess or a "surely": 田中さんだろう (that must be Tanaka). じゃないか presents what you can plainly see: 田中さんじゃないか (why, it's Tanaka!).
よね checks a belief you hold with the listener: 明日休みだよね (tomorrow's a day off, right?). じゃないか pushes the point as obvious, often with surprise or blame.
かな wonders, unsure: おいしいかな (I wonder if it's good). じゃないか is certain: おいしいじゃないか (hey, it's good!).

mistakes.bad: なんだ、田中[たなか]さんだ{じゃないか}。
mistakes.good: なんだ、田中[たなか]さん{じゃないか}。
mistakes.note: No だ before じゃないか; it attaches straight to the noun.

mistakes.bad: このケーキ、おいしく{じゃないか}。
mistakes.good: このケーキ、おいしい{じゃないか}。
mistakes.note: じゃないか is not negation, so the adjective keeps its plain form, not the く of おいしくない.

skills.tip: Can you replace it with "hey, look: ...!" or "..., didn't I?" without any "not"? Then it is the particle じゃないか.
